messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify inorder traversal prints keys in sorted order for a minimal nontrivial BST (root and two children).
test_metadata.rationale: This test ensures the function traverses both left and right subtrees, exercises all recursive calls, and prints keys in correct order, covering the full non-NULL path.

dependencies.name: insert
dependencies.signature: struct node* insert(struct node* node, int key)
dependencies.reason: Used to build the BST for test setup

dependencies.name: helper_build_tree
dependencies.signature: struct node* helper_build_tree(int* values, int size)
dependencies.reason: Utility to construct BST from array

dependencies.name: helper_free_tree
dependencies.reason: Utility to free BST after test

assertions.name: assert_tree_inorder_equal
assertions.purpose: Verify that inorder traversal output matches expected sorted array
assertions.usage: After calling inorder, check output order

utilities.name: helper_build_tree
utilities.purpose: Builds a BST from an array of values
utilities.usage: Setup phase to create test tree

utilities.name: helper_free_tree
utilities.purpose: Frees all nodes in the BST

setup_requirements.initial_state: No tree exists; will build a BST with root 2, left child 1, right child 3

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: Pointer to root of BST with keys 2 (root), 1 (left), 3 (right)
primary_function_args.rationale: Minimal tree that exercises both left and right recursion

side_effects.effect: Keys printed to stdout in sorted order: '1 2 3 '
side_effects.observable_via: Intercept output or use assert_tree_inorder_equal to compare traversal result

invariants_maintained: No memory is allocated or freed by inorder

assertions_required.description: Verify inorder traversal yields sorted array of keys
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Traversal order is incorrect or function does not visit all nodes

memory_to_free: BST root and all nodes (via helper_free_tree)
cleanup_requirements.final_state: All dynamically allocated memory freed; no resource leaks

operation_sequence: Build BST with values [2,1,3] using helper_build_tree
edge_cases_to_note: Tree with only root (no children) would not exercise both left and right recursion
Empty tree (root == NULL) is not covered by this path

path_coverage_analysis.description: Non-NULL root; traverses left, prints key, traverses right (full recursion)

integration_test_suggestions: Test inorder on larger BSTs to confirm scalability and correctness.
Test inorder after insertions and deletions to ensure traversal remains correct.
